lead: Nebraska plumbing deals with cold winters, hard water and river flooding. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from Omaha to Lincoln and beyond.
risk: frozen pipes, hard water scale and flooded basements
risk_short: frozen pipes, hard water and flooding
why: Nebraska water is often hard, scaling up water heaters and fixtures. Many homes have basements with sump pumps.
Winters freeze pipes, and river flooding, as in 2019, damages homes. Nebraska has no statewide plumber license; cities such as Omaha and Lincoln license plumbers.
tips: Test your sump pump before spring.
areas: Calls come from Omaha, Lincoln, Bellevue, Grand Island, Kearney and rural Nebraska.

faq.q: Do plumbers need a license in Nebraska?
faq.a: There is no statewide plumber license. Cities such as Omaha and Lincoln license plumbers and issue permits.
